funder.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan

record.rationale: Barangay 83 (Paraiso) was one of three places where a 2014 independent survey found total mangrove mortality (Inquirer Opinion, Jun 2014). A DENR-assisted planting in early 2014 was killed by Typhoons Ruby and Seniang that December (UP Open University study, 2022); the community replanted with funding from Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Journal of Environmental Management, 2025).
record.planned_action_detail: About 30,000 seedlings on 4 ha, 2015-2018 (Journal of Environmental Management, 2025); OISCA paid about 15 workers ₱8 per seedling potted and ₱7 per seedling outplanted (UP Open University study, 2022).
record.expected_outcome: Restore the mangrove fringe that protected the barangay before the typhoon (Journal of Environmental Management, 2025). No numeric target was published.
record.known_unknowns: This is not an MBFDP site: no source ties Paraiso to the ₱1 billion program. A resident says the planting was done “without a single cent of support from the government” (Mongabay, 2023), while DENR assisted the failed 2014 planting (UP Open University study, 2022). The polygon is the OpenStreetMap mangrove stand in Barangay 83, not the planted boundary. Reconstructed on 2026-10-04 from public sources; this record was not locked at the time, so its hash proves only that the reconstruction has not changed since.
